binders: p, an arbitrary nonnegative real number.
hypotheses: p is at most 1; together with its NNReal type, this means 0 ≤ p ≤ 1.
conclusions: The pushforward of the Boolean Bernoulli distribution with parameter p under the map true ↦ 1 and false ↦ -1 equals the corresponding pushforward of the Bernoulli distribution with parameter 1/2 if and only if p = 1/2.
mathematical_definitions: Define f : Bool → Real by f(true) = 1 and f(false) = -1.
The Bernoulli PMF with parameter p assigns probability p to true and 1 - p to false.
The fixed reference PMF is the pushforward under f of the Bernoulli PMF with parameter 1/2; equivalently, it assigns probability 1/2 to each of 1 and -1.
PMF.map f denotes the pushforward of a discrete probability mass function along f.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every valid Bernoulli parameter p, encoding true as 1 and false as -1 produces the symmetric two-point distribution on {-1, 1} exactly when p is one half.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The parameter is restricted to NNReal and is assumed at most 1, so it lies in the probability interval [0, 1].
The assertion concerns exact equality of probability mass functions, not merely equality of expectations, moments, or supports.
The sign map takes the two Boolean outcomes to the distinct real values 1 and -1, so the pushforward retains the Bernoulli parameter and the reverse implication is not vacuous.
The proposition concerns a single two-point Bernoulli law; it does not assert independence, describe repeated trials, or characterize more general random variables.
The proof argument hp and the fixed proof LocalDef005 certify that the Bernoulli parameters are valid; the particular proof terms do not alter the resulting mathematical distributions.
